rationale: Iteration 9 scored 880.7, below iteration 8's 913.5. Narrowing wheel_track from 0.12 to 0.11 m cut slalom finishes from 18/20 to 15/20, raised slalom off-track ends from 2 to 5, and raised slalom control_effort from 14.3 to 15.1. Oval and s-bend were unchanged. The faster turn rate therefore overcorrected on the alternating bends, so the track-width lever is a net loss. I am reverting to the iteration 8 design, which is the best evidence so far: oval 20/20, s-bend 20/20, slalom 18/20, with oscillation of 0.24 to 0.32, well under the 0.5 warning level. Everything else stays as in iteration 8 (sensor y 0.08 at the top of the allowed range, sensor spread of 0.04 m, sensor_size 0.016, kp 5.5, kd 1.5, ki 0.01, base_speed 1.2, mass 0.6, wheel_radius 0.03, line_loss last_direction). I am not making a blind change, because the per-track ceiling is about 940 to 950 and the remaining gap is the slalom tail. Expected result: a score close to 913, with slalom finishes of 16 to 19 of 20. Hypotheses: (a) the slalom off-track ends are now a steering-authority limit at the sharpest alternating bends, so the next lever is kd up to about 1.7 to contain overshoot at kp 5.5; (b) if oscillation stays low and slalom still misses, a mild kp increase to about 5.8 is worth testing; (c) the time term (about 20 points per track) can be raised by base_speed of about 1.25, but only if oval and s-bend completion hold at 1.0. Next measurements: completion, progress, completion_time, max_error, rms_error, line_loss_events, steering_oscillation and control_effort per track, so I can tell whether the slalom failures are overshoot or lost authority.
